label: <DEL> step of short sequences, favoring certain first tokens
explanation: Reset-gate unit that fires almost only at the delimiter step (97% of activation mass; 12% of all <DEL> steps), where the model must start outputting original token 0. It is strongly gated by sequence length: active on 15% of <DEL> steps at L=3, 6% at L=4, 2% at L=5, and almost never at L>=6. Within short sequences it depends on the first original token (the token about to be output). First tokens i, d, l, m, h, 0, x, 2, o, w raise the firing rate; i gives the strongest activations, and every top example begins with i. This looks like a graded combination of shortness and first-token identity rather than a crisp rule. The predicate (L=3, or L<=5 with a favored first token) gets dev F1 0.74 and mass recall 0.89. Minor firing (3% of mass) happens on original-phase inputs p/q at t=2-3 in short sequences. It never fires in the copy phase, at t<2, or on repeated tokens.
